implementation_notes: The message is a @dataclass(frozen=True) value and the mapper is a module with two pure functions - to_message(order: Order) -> OrderMessage and from_message(m: OrderMessage) -> Order; dataclasses.asdict covers the mechanical part only where names and units happen to agree, and json.dumps/json.loads (or the client library's serialiser, e.g. a Celery task payload) own the wire encoding. What replaces the mapper class is that pair of functions: one module importable by the endpoint and imported by neither the domain module nor the consumer's business code. Keep them total and explicit, and leave validation of foreign payloads as a separate, deliberate step.
pitfalls: dataclasses.asdict recurses: pointed at an aggregate it will serialise associations (or a lazy object) that the message must not publish.
A dict-shaped message keyed by strings makes typos silent (m['total_minor'] versus m['totalMinor']) - pass a typed message object across the boundary.
Frozen dataclasses are shallow: a message holding a list still lets a consumer mutate it, so copy or tuple-ify collections in the mapper.

variants.name: Pydantic v2 message model with aliases and validators
variants.implementation_notes: Declare the message as a BaseModel and let pydantic own the wire half: Field(validation_alias=...)/serialization_alias name the keys, validators normalise units and reject malformed payloads, and model_validate/model_dump_json convert between the wire shape and Python data - the mapper collapses into a from_domain classmethod plus the model's field declarations. Choose it when payloads are untrusted or the contract is documented but not enforced; the cost is a dependency plus the discipline to keep business invariants out of model validators.
pitfalls: Pydantic coercion is liberal ("12" becomes 12): use strict models or strict field types where a malformed message must fail instead of being repaired.
model_dump in Python mode leaves datetime, Decimal and UUID as Python objects; use mode="json" before handing the payload to a serialiser.
Validators are the wrong home for domain invariants: they run on the wire shape, so business rules placed there are bypassed by every other entry point.
